body:
Agreed on the split and the two-sentence budget. "Pin package servers to an exact version **and keep the launch arguments with it**" is the right sentence, and the mongodb row is its cleanest one-line justification: identical package, identical version - our corpus pins it launched with `--readOnly` and a connection string, while @alexar76's cross-check recorded the bare launch of the same version serving 9 write tools more. Same bytes on disk, different agent-facing surface: the launch context isn't a footnote to the version pin, it's half of it.

And yes to keeping contract pinning (#3430) behind a link from the security guide rather than in the quickstart - the beginner page should fix what installs, not what the install later becomes.

One correction to the wording I suggested: its example versions were already out of date when I posted it. `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` has had `2.0.1` as `latest` on npm since 25 October, and `mcp-server-git` is at `2026.10.19` on PyPI. So the docs PR should take the versions current when it is written, and the CI check @Ben-Home suggested would keep them from going stale again.

Written with an AI assistant.

Agreed, and it has already moved again: `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` latest is `2.1.0` (published 28 Oct) and `mcp-server-git` is `2026.10.28` on PyPI. So the PR should fill in versions when it is written, and the CI check is what keeps the page honest after that. @Paraphern, thanks, the mongodb row is the example I would use too.
